subject: Discovery recap: recommended models, perf links, and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari.patel@lumenix.ai>; Priya Rao <priya.rao@lumenix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: recommended models, perf links, and pilot next steps

Hi Ari / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: real-time summarization and clinical-document enrichment for downstream search; ~600 concurrent users at peak expected.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end ~250–300ms for short responses (avg 60–120 tokens).
- Throughput requirement: ~120 TPS sustained during spikes; burst to 250 TPS for short windows.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in downstream docs; prefer VPC/private deployment for pilot review.

Redwood-recommended slate (initial pilot)
- redwood/rosetta-13B-quant — best cost/perf for extractive QA and short summaries; strong p95 latency on A100s.
- open/ceres-7B-v2 — lower-cost baseline for non-critical enrichment paths; good throughput when sharded.
- redwood/atlas-30B-8bit — higher-quality fall-back for complex summarization tests (use selectively for longer sequences).

What I’m attaching / sharing
- Benchmarks: a Redwood-run snapshot of model throughput and latency across target hardware (see attachment and Drive link).
- Prompt set: the canonical prompt pack we used for the tests (prompt_set_lumenix.jsonl).
- Redwood-verified performance profiles: CSV with p50/p95/p99 and TPS figures by model/hardware.

Quality/regression notes
- We flagged two prompt classes where the 13B quantized model shows brittle hallucination behavior on nested instructions; we recommend a small eval set (50 examples) that mirrors your worst-case docs.
- We'll wire up continuous evals during the pilot and surface regressions to your team and ours via the Console.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Ben to share full bench links, perf CSV, and recommended runtime configs (today).
2) Lumenix to confirm acceptance criteria for the 50-case regression pack (by Tue).
3) Schedule pilot kickoff (VPC review + reserved capacity options) — suggested window Aug 23–27.

If that timeline works, I’ll create a mutual action plan and loop in our security/infra folks for the VPC checklist.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: lumenix_benchmark_v1.html (html report), prompt_set_lumenix.jsonl (prompt lines), redwood_verified_profiles.csv (perf table)
From: Ari Patel <ari.patel@lumenix.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@lumenix.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: recommended models, perf links, and pilot next steps

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Throughput: the 120 TPS is user-facing inference calls; the back-end enrichment pipeline can absorb some batching but we need to guarantee p95 latency for the user-facing path.
- Data: yes, PHI. SOC 2 + encrypted logs are mandatory — can you share the SOC 2 certificate and audit log retention policy?
- Pilot: we’d like the initial pilot to run in our VPC (can you share the VPC onboarding checklist and required firewall rules?).

Also, Priya asked whether we can try the 13B-quant and the 7B in parallel and compare quality on our 50-case evaluation pack; if you can share the perf CSV and prompt pack today that helps prioritize.

Ari
Ari Patel
CTO, Lumenix

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: recommended models, perf links, and pilot next steps

Ari / Priya — forwarding the bench outputs and a short interpretation below. Files attached and Drive link in the header.

Attachment highlights
- redwood_verified_profiles.csv: per-model rows with p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) measured on the A100-80GB pool and concurrent TPS measured in our continuous-batching runner.
- lumenix_benchmark_v1.html: interactive trace viewer with the sample traces we ran using your sample prompts (anonymized).
- prompt_set_lumenix.jsonl: canonical eval + regression set (50 primary cases + 20 fuzz variants).

Key numbers (from the CSV, median of three runs)
- redwood/rosetta-13B-quant (A100-80GB): sustained TPS ~140; p50 32ms, p95 220ms, p99 380ms. Memory headroom supports 2x burst with autoscale.
- open/ceres-7B-v2 (A10G sharded x2): sustained TPS ~320; p50 18ms, p95 140ms, p99 240ms. Lower quality on nested instruction examples.
- redwood/atlas-30B-8bit (A100-80GB): sustained TPS ~55; p50 48ms, p95 360ms, p99 720ms — recommended as a selective fallback for complex docs.

Cost/operational notes
- For the user-facing path we recommend running rosetta-13B-quant as primary with ceres-7B as a low-cost background enrichment path. Use atlas-30B as a gated fallback for a subset of longer documents.
- We’ll enable prefix caching for repeated patient-note headers to drop p95 by ~20% in synthetic tests.

Quality/regression guardrails
- We’ve added a regression monitor tied to the prompt_set_lumenix.jsonl; we’ll fail the run if hallucination rate increases by >5% vs baseline on the 50-case pack.
- Suggested evaluation cadence: nightly runs during pilot; weekly summary to Priya and Marissa.

Next operational items (action owners)
- Jordan: create MAP and propose pilot dates (in thread).
- Lumenix: confirm the 50-case list and the acceptance thresholds (Ari/Priya).
- Ben/Infra: send VPC onboarding checklist and SOC 2 PDF (we’ll attach from compliance).

I’ve attached the three files and pushed the interactive report and CSV to Drive (link above). Let me know if you want a short walkthrough — I can demo the trace viewer and show where the p99 outliers come from.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: lumenix_benchmark_v1.html, prompt_set_lumenix.jsonl, redwood_verified_profiles.csv
